sources.note: Phonology chapter concerns Pukur only. §1.4.1: 'The Baga Kakisa / Sobané, located between the Pongo River and Cape Verga (villages of Sobané, Marara)'; 'BERLINER (2013) reports that while individuals from Baga Kalum, Koba, and Kakisa/Sobané continue to identify as Baga, they no longer speak their native language'. Nothing on Sobané prosody.

sources.citation: Lamp, Frederick John. 2021 [2016, rev. June 2021]. Baga Tshi-Tem Dictionary (Guinea) / Po-lokuloku pə tshə-Baka tshi-Tem. 132 pp. PDF, Cataloging Africana.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Front matter 'Intonation' (PDF p. 7): 'The accent generally falls on the initial syllable, although often there is no accent distinguishable. When the accent falls on a following syllable, it is indicated in bold.' This is stated for Baga tshi-Tem (Sitemu). Sobané appears only as 'Bkk = Baga Kakisa (Sobané)', one of four other dialect groups from which ~30 selected culture words are included 'for the reason that no dictionaries exist for these dialects'; no prosodic statement specific to Sobané.
